pages.title: Consultations - NPT Council
pages.text:
Consultations
Read our
privacy statement
Thank you for visiting Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council's consultation page which will allow you to comment and provide feedback on topics relevant to Neath Port Talbot.
We look forward to reading your responses to our consultations.
Draft Taxi Licensing Policy consultation
Neath Port Talbot Council is responsible for licensing hackney carriage and private hire drivers, vehicles and operators. The Council’s licensing arrangements are intended to protect public safety and ensure that licensed services are safe, suitable and properly regulated.
The Council is reviewing its Taxi Licensing Policy, which sets out the standards, requirements and procedures that generally apply when it considers licence applications and regulates existing licence holders.
We value the views of residents, the licensed trade, partner organisations and other interested parties, and we would like to hear what you think about our revised Taxi Licensing Policy. A copy of the revised policy is available with the proposed changes highlighted in red.
We welcome any comments you may have on the revised policy.
Downloads
Taxi Licensing Policy - revised August 2026 (PDF 5.94 MB)
The consultation will close at 12:00 noon on Thursday 26 November 2026.

20/11/2026
Swansea favourite Kev Johns finally rings out the good news!
It’s always a special moment when a cancer patient rings the all-clear bell but for Kev Johns it was doubly so!
20/11/2026
Notice of board meeting - 26 November 2026
Notice is hereby given that a meeting of Swansea Bay University Health Board will be held on Thursday, 26 November 2026 at 10:30am In the Millennium Room at Headquarters, One Talbot Gateway, Baglan, SA12 7BR.
20/11/2026
Spotlight on Gorseinon Hospital at November's health board meeting
The future role of Swansea’s Gorseinon Hospital as a vibrant community healthcare hub will be considered by health board members next week as part of its decision around the potential permanent transfer of inpatient beds to Singleton Hospital.
18/11/2026
Digital food app a success as it serves up more than just tasty meals
A successful meal ordering system across two Swansea Bay hospitals is delivering more empty plates, less food waste and happier patients.
16/11/2026
Solar farm's success passes the £6million mark at fifth anniversary
Morriston Hospital’s groundbreaking solar farm has amassed over £6million in power savings as it marks its fifth anniversary.
13/11/2026
Important Notice - Global Microsoft Outage
Despite a global Microsoft Outage, no major issues have been reported with any of our services.
12/11/2026
Warm and Healthy Homes pilot brings free energy and wellbeing support to Briton Ferry residents
A new partnership is bringing health and housing support together to help people in Briton Ferry stay warmer, reduce their energy costs and improve their health and wellbeing.
10/11/2026
Carpentry, coastline and countryside helping patients recover from traumatic brain injuries
A Swansea Bay service is making the most of its landscape to help patients recover from a traumatic brain injury.
09/11/2026
GP puts his foot down to look after planet as well as patients
A Swansea Bay GP is practicing what he preaches as he looks after the planet as well as his patients.
05/11/2026
People supported back into work and education through new OT service
A new service is helping to support people to overcome challenges that are impacting their social or working lives.
03/11/2026
New Nature Prescription booklets aim to boost wellbeing across Swansea Bay
Guides showcase beauty spots and ways to explore the natural world.
03/11/2026
Podiatry project which drastically reduced waiting times earns national attention
A community-based podiatry project has received national recognition after reducing waiting times of up to two years to just two weeks for patients.
29/10/2026
Respiratory nurses saving lives on the home front
Two Swansea Bay paediatric nurses are helping save children’s lives through highlighting poor living conditions which exacerbate respiratory diseases.
26/10/2026
Practice websites - temporary disruption
Three GP practices contacting patients.
26/10/2026
Former The Traitors finalist inspires mental health patients during visit to unique Cae Felin project
Andrew Jenkins, who has fought his own battles with mental health, dropped in to pick crops and enjoy a cuppa.
23/10/2026
Swansea Bay Apprentice Academy celebrates 10 years of developing talent
Swansea Bay University Health Board's Apprentice Academy is today (October 23) celebrating a decade of people, progress and partnerships.
22/10/2026
Swansea Bay oncologists lead world first radiotherapy trial for patients with inoperable stomach cancer
The trial is funded through a £3 million grant from Cancer Research UK and will involve hundreds of patients from across the UK.
14/10/2026
Super-fit Rachel gets vaccinated after losing a stone while sick with flu
Being young and physically fit, Swansea Bay physiotherapist Rachel Walsh never saw any point in having the flu vaccine. That was until earlier this year when she became so ill with the virus that she lost a stone in weight and took more than a month to fully recover.
10/10/2026
Conversations over cuppas in the shed help boost men's mental health
A dedicated area for men to dig deep in more ways than one has been unveiled at an agricultural project based on Swansea Bay University Health Board land.
09/10/2026
Pelvic health physio education sessions in running for national award
A prevention-focused project which created community sessions to empower and educate women on pelvic health has been shortlisted for a national award.

pages.title: Age Connects Neath & Port Talbot | Community Outreach Hubs
pages.text:
Cymraeg
Donate
COMMUNITY OUTREACH HUBS
Community Outreach Hubs
Community
Outreach Hubs
We know that recent changes and challenges within Neath Port Talbot that has seen further closures of local shops, post offices, chapels, churches, local day services and a reduction in public transport directly influence an older persons independence and quality of life.
We have several Community Outreach Hubs located across the County Borough, and are always looking for new accessible locations. These act as an extension to our current services and ensure that local people have direct access to our services. Currently we our
weekly
Outreach Hubs take place at the following venues:
Neath Community Centre (Orchard Street, Neath) - Monday's 10:00 - 12:30
Bertha Road Community Centre, Margam - Tuesday's 10:30 - 12:30
Pontardawe Library - Thursday's 13:00 - 15:00
The aim of the Outreach Services is to provide a holistic intervention programme to increase prevention and provide early intervention of physical and emotional support. Activities are fun and user led as we aim to create a positive experience of ageing, with local residents feeling involved, appreciated, more confident and active within their community. Last year,
we delivered 600 Community Outreach activity sessions.
Our Outreach Hubs can help you live life to the full by providing a wide range of self-sustaining activities that encourage and improve physical and emotional health and well-being. We also work in partnership with a wide range of providers and local groups who offer community support and are confident that there is something for everyone to enjoy. Activities are delivered through various methods and services including the following:
Information and advice
This service covers topics including welfare benefits, health, housing, free legal advice, employment, consumer, leisure and learning. Support is also provided on complex issues such as future living arrangements, care home fees, equity release and funeral arrangements
Health and well-being
Activities include physical activity classes, movement to music sessions, walking groups, healthy eating workshops, reminiscence, mindfulness sessions and health promotion information
Creative Activities
An opportunity to participate in a range of art and craft activities, creative writing, singing and music etc. to learn a new skill, reduce loneliness and improve emotional well-being
Digital inclusion
We provide digital inclusion support in a fun and practical environment, helping people improve confidence and access to services. A range of digital equipment is available or you can bring along your own equipment to our gadget drop in sessions
Excursions
We organise regular day trips to places of interest and various tourist attractions which are individually priced. Please get in touch for information on upcoming dates and destinations
Foot Care Service
This service helps to reduce falls and improve independence and is delivered by fully trained staff and volunteers, all of whom are retired nurses and/or healthcare professionals. A number of our Community Outreach Hubs host regular clinics, as well as a regular drop in service
In addition to formal outreach services, we also attend public places such as shopping centres and supermarkets throughout the County Borough to promote our range of services and products.

pages.name: Community Lives: community projects
pages.title: Community Projects - Community Lives
pages.text:
Our Community Projects
We are very proud of the wide range of activities, groups and events we offer across our localities and networks, helping to strengthen wellbeing and build connections among the people we support and the wider community.
If you are interested in any of our community projects and would like more information, please get in touch:
info@communitylives.org
Camera Club
4
5
Community Lives organises an accessible and inclusive
Camera Club for adults with a learning disability.
Sessions are held once a month, alternating between field trips for inspiration and workshops where technical skills are developed and practised.
Camera Club is facilitated by a professional photographer and supported by our Participation and Engagement Officer. We work in partnership with Y Storfa and Swansea Council's Cultural Services to support the development of this creative group.
Better Together Choir
4
5
Community Lives and Drive Cymru formed a partnership in 2024 to develop and organise an
inclusive
and
accessible
choir in Neath Port Talbot for adults with a learning disability.
The choir practises every Wednesday from 5pm to 7pm and performs at various events throughout the year.
This lively and uplifting group encourages teamwork, learning and personal development.
Clwb Croeso
4
5
Community Lives organises a weekly
creative and social group
in Neath Port Talbot every Monday from 11am to 1pm, offering opportunities to enjoy arts and crafts, music and social activities to the people we support and the local community.
Organised by one of our Registered Care Homes, this group provides an opportunity for people to come together in their local community and take part in a range of inclusive and accessible activities.
Locality & Network Activities
Across our
localities and networks
, we offer a diverse range of activities that are informed by the needs, interests and aspirations of the people we support.
These activities help to improve health and wellbeing, encourage learning and personal development, and strengthen connections within their local communities.
Swansea (Localities 1, 2 & 4)
Locality 1 Monthly Meetups, Locality 2 Coffee Morning, Locality 4 Pub and Pool Night, Monthly Walks, Gardening Group, Locality 4 Go Explore.
Seasonal day trips and events are also held across all localities in Swansea.
Neath Port Talbot (Networks 5 & 6)
Network 5 Coffee Morning with Bingo, Quiz, Arts and Crafts and the Tonna Disco and Karaoke. Network 6 Better Together Choir.
Seasonal day trips and events are held across both networks in Neath Port Talbot.
We believe communities are
enriched
by the inclusion and participation of all people.
At Community Lives, our
commitment to community development
creates
opportunities for connection,
friendship
and support.
Our groups aim to help people develop skills, pursue their
interests
and increase local community resources.
4
5
Through workshops and questionnaires, we have been guided by the interests of the people we support to create activities and opportunities that reflect what people want.
In Locality 4, this has included a Gardening Group (Been There Dug That) and an events group, Locality 4 Go Explore.
4
5
In Neath Port Talbot, the people we
support
and their staff organise a range of inclusive, welcoming activities and events across the area. Opportunities to connect through shared activities and interests help people build valued and supportive relationships.
Tenant Participation
The people we support have a range of opportunities to participate in meetings, forums and presentations, both within Community Lives and with our external partners. This ensures their voices and lived experiences are heard and used to inform and drive improvements across the sector.
Community Lives Board Members
We ensure our Board of Management includes people we support and offer Trustee positions to promote diverse perspectives and lived experience at all levels of governance.
Tenant Lives Group
Members of our Senior Management Team meet quarterly with our Tenant Lives Group representatives to discuss important updates, gather feedback and plan together. This helps us remain user-led and values-focused.
Better Together Leadership Group
The leadership group brings together organisations from the third sector, housing, voluntary services, supported living providers and people with lived experience to plan and organise activities in the NPT area. Collaboration and co-production are at the heart of these meetings, helping to shape inclusive and meaningful opportunities within the community.
West Glamorgan Regional Partnership Task & Finish Group
Our supported individuals are involved in task and finish groups organised by the West Glamorgan Regional Partnership Board. Through these groups, the people we support can share their views and help shape recommendations on topics such as transport, easy-read information, community inclusion, and getting the right care and support.
Swansea Council Steering Group
We work closely with Swansea Council's Steering Group for Supported Living, which enables the people we support to take part in meetings and presentations to share how they have come together as a locality and network to influence services and support within their local community.
